key_insight: VideoAtlas represents long videos as a hierarchical, lossless spatial–temporal grid (an "atlas") that lets models navigate and query content with logarithmic compute cost, removing the need for captions or heavy preprocessing.
problem_solved: Overcomes two bottlenecks in video-language scaling: lossy, low-fidelity video representations and long-context pipelines that collapse video into text, preventing scalable, high-fidelity long-form video reasoning and retrieval.
method: Hierarchical grid (atlas) representation: tile videos into multi-scale spatial–temporal cells that preserve visual fidelity and provide an at-a-glance overview.
Coarse-to-fine, indexed navigation: multi-resolution indexing enables targeted access so queries cost grows logarithmically with video length rather than linearly.
Task-agnostic, preprocessing-free interface: supports direct visual navigation and retrieval without captioning or task-specific preprocessing, enabling plug-and-play downstream use.
impact: Makes long-form video understanding and interactive applications (QA, retrieval, editing) computationally feasible at scale while preserving visual fidelity. Practitioners can integrate long videos into models with much lower compute and without lossy summarization.
visual_elements: Hierarchical atlas diagram: a video timeline overlaid with nested grid tiles showing coarse-to-fine zoom and reachable cells.
Compute-scaling chart: comparison of linear (traditional) vs logarithmic (VideoAtlas) compute cost as video length increases.
Pipeline comparison: side-by-side flowchart of caption/preprocessing-based pipelines vs VideoAtlas's navigable, lossless access.
Use-case icons: examples like interactive QA, retrieval, and video editing with arrows showing fast targeted access into the atlas.
paper_title: VideoAtlas: Navigating Long-Form Video in Logarithmic Compute
paper_authors: Mohamed Eltahir, Ali Habibullah, Yazan Alshoibi, Lama Ayash, Tanveer Hussain
